title: Tariff Clerk's Worksheet: The Storage Charge for a Billing Period
content:
The charge for the period is the daily rate the programme posts, applied to the bushels standing in store that are free to move and to every day of the period: the daily rate multiplied by the billed bushels multiplied by the days billed, that product rounded to the nearest cent, and where the product falls under the programme's period minimum the period minimum is charged instead. This worksheet covers Grain Storage and Conditioning Agreements.

## The quantities the worksheet reads

**The bushels.** The bushels standing in store are backed out of the storage account and never read off the agreement header, being the bushels taken into store under the agreement less the bushels taken off for shrink and less the bushels loaded out, and the bushels free to move are those bushels less the bushels pledged against an outstanding warehouse receipt.

**The period.** A billing period runs the programme's period length in calendar days beginning the day after the date storage was last billed and paid through, and only a period whose last day has already passed is billed. The days billed are every day of that period.

**The rate.** The daily rate is the rate the programme posts for each bushel for each day. It is worked out in full and carried to five decimal places before it is applied to the bushels and the days, and it is never less than nothing.

**The floor.** The programme's period minimum is the floor under the charge for any one billing period.

## The charge, worked through on hypothetical figures

Take an agreement whose programme posts a daily rate of 0.00200 for each bushel for each day, whose period length is 30 calendar days and whose period minimum is 30.00, with the date storage was last billed and paid through standing at 31 March.

1. The period runs the 30 calendar days beginning the day after 31 March, that is from 1 April through 30 April, and it is billed because 30 April has passed.
2. The storage account shows 14000 bushels taken into store, 120 bushels taken off for shrink and 1000 bushels loaded out, so the bushels standing in store are 12880; with 880 bushels pledged against an outstanding receipt, the bushels free to move are 12000.
3. The rate carried to five decimal places is 0.00200.
4. Two thousandths of a dollar multiplied by 12000 bushels multiplied by 30 days is 720.00, which rounded to the nearest cent is 720.00.
5. That figure stands above the period minimum of 30.00, so 720.00 is the charge for the period.

## A second hypothetical, where the floor governs

On the same programme-posted rate of 0.00200 and the same period of 30 days, an agreement with 300 bushels free to move gives two thousandths of a dollar multiplied by 300 bushels multiplied by 30 days, which is 18.00. That falls under the period minimum of 30.00, so 30.00 is charged for the period.

## Basis questions answered

**Why is the quantity backed out of the storage account rather than read off the agreement?** Because the account carries every movement: what came in, what came off for shrink and what went out. The worksheet reads those three and works the quantity from them.

**A period whose last day is still to come.** Only a period whose last day has already passed is billed, so a period still running is not yet a period the worksheet prices.
